no29-1797-04-13.summary: King reports on Sweden: under the late regency (Duke Karl's guardianship, which ended when Gustav IV Adolf took over the government on 1 Nov 1796; Svenskt biografiskt lexikon, 'Gustav IV Adolf') Swedish policy favoured France; the young King is more national in outlook and French influence at Stockholm is less, so the President's answer to the Swedish overtures, declining them 'for the present', should be well received there. The overture is the Swedish minister Engeström's proposition to Thomas Pinckney, which Pickering answered through King on 17 Sept 1796 (Pickering to John Adams, 24 Sept 1798, Founders Online, Adams Papers 99-02-02-3023). The despatch then turns, in clear, to the Maryland Bank Stock, Captain Home and seamen.
no29-1797-04-13.en:
NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Great Britain, vol. 5 (microfilm M30 roll 4), frames 0092 (right page) to 0096 (right page); the code is on 0092 only
([image](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/dc-metro/rg-059/603720/M30/M30-004/M30-004-0092.jpg)). A clerk's copy received
by the Department of State. The recipient is Timothy Pickering, Secretary of State. The coded words are bare: nothing is written
over them, and no decipherment was found on this frame or the next. No printed text of this despatch was found (see NOTES.md, Prior work).

Marks: words decoded from the code are in italics; the rest is in clear on the page. [?word] marks a word that rests on a code
value read from the context of this letter alone (key grade I). Each such word is a hole until another occurrence or a clear text
confirms it. [e] marks a letter supplied.

no59-1797-12-23.summary: King reports that the British Cabinet has rejected a French peace proposal made through Talleyrand, the price of which was a bribe of a million sterling to the Directors, ministers and others; he vouches for the information but asks that it not be published as coming from him.
